message.content:
In the Go repo at /bench/home/work (memos project), answer two questions with exact paths and line numbers. Search only Go code (server/, store/, internal/, cmd/, proto/gen counts too but note it separately).

Q1: Find EVERY method declaration named RunOnce (grep 'func (.*) RunOnce'). For each declarer type, report path:line. Then find all call sites of RunOnce in non-test production Go code (grep '\.RunOnce(') and report which declarers are actually invoked and from where (caller path:line). Note ones that are never called from production code.

Q2: Count all distinct method declarations named Close in backend Go code (grep -rn 'func (.*) Close(' across store/ server/ internal/ cmd/ — exclude web/ and _test.go files; you may exclude proto/gen generated code but say whether any exist there). List each declarer type with path:line. Then find which Close methods are actually CALLED from non-test server/production code (grep '\.Close()' in cmd/, server/, store/ non-test files) and match callers to declarers — e.g. store.Store.Close called in cmd/main.go. Report caller path:line for each invoked declarer. Be careful: many .Close() calls are on stdlib types (http response bodies, files) — only count calls that resolve to the repo's own Close declarations.

- graphify: Use for any question about a codebase, its architecture, file relationships, or project content — especially when graphify-out/ exists, where the question should be treated as a graphify query first. Turns any input (code, docs, papers, images, videos) into a persistent knowledge graph with god nodes, community detection, and query/path/explain tools.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
Findings below. Note: `proto/gen/...` (Go generated code lives under `/bench/home/work/proto/gen/`) contains **zero** `RunOnce` or `Close` method declarations — nothing to report there for either question.

## Q1 — `RunOnce`

**Declarations (2 total, both on a type named `Runner` in different packages):**

| Declarer | Path:line |
|---|---|
| `*memopayload.Runner` | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` |
| `*s3presign.Runner` | `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:43` |

**Call sites (`.RunOnce(`) — 2, both resolving to `s3presign.Runner`:**

- `/bench/home/work/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:36` — self-call from `(*s3presign.Runner).Run`, on the 12h ticker tick.
- `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:163` — `s3presignRunner.RunOnce(ctx)` inside `(*Server).startBackgroundRunners`, an eager run at startup before the goroutine loop.

**Never invoked:** `(*memopayload.Runner).RunOnce` at `server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:27` is dead code from production. Its constructor `memopayload.NewRunner` also has zero call sites anywhere in the repo (including tests). Only the package-level helper `memopayload.RebuildMemoPayload` is used, from `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/memo_service.go:108` and `:447`. So the `Runner` struct, `NewRunner`, and `RunOnce` in that package are entirely unreferenced.

## Q2 — `Close`

**Declarations in `store/`, `server/`, `internal/`, `cmd/`, excluding `_test.go` — 6 total** (`internal/` and `cmd/` have none):

| Declarer | Path:line |
|---|---|
| `*v1.SSEHub` | `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/sse_hub.go:99` |
| `*cache.Cache` | `/bench/home/work/store/cache/cache.go:187` |
| `*mysql.DB` | `/bench/home/work/store/db/mysql/mysql.go:47` |
| `*postgres.DB` | `/bench/home/work/store/db/postgres/postgres.go:46` |
| `*sqlite.DB` | `/bench/home/work/store/db/sqlite/sqlite.go:67` |
| `*store.Store` | `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:72` |

(Excluded as `_test.go`: `MemoFilterTestContext.Close` and `AttachmentFilterTestContext.Close` at `/bench/home/work/store/test/filter_helpers_test.go:200` and `:282`.)

**Callers that resolve to repo-owned `Close` declarations:**

- `*store.Store.Close` ← `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:146` (in `(*Server).Shutdown`, the real production path; `cmd/memos/main.go:101` reaches it indirectly via `s.Shutdown(ctx)` — main.go never calls `Store.Close()` itself). Also ← `/bench/home/work/server/router/api/v1/test/test_helper.go:66` (`ts.Store.Close()`), a test-support file that is not named `_test.go`.
- `*cache.Cache.Close` ← `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:74`, `:75`, `:76` (the three caches `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`).
- `*v1.SSEHub.Close` ← `/bench/home/work/server/server.go:206` (in `closeLongLivedConnections`).
- `*mysql.DB.Close` / `*postgres.DB.Close` / `*sqlite.DB.Close` ← reached **only indirectly** through the interface call at `/bench/home/work/store/store.go:78` (`return s.driver.Close()`). The `Driver` interface declares `Close() error` at `/bench/home/work/store/driver.go:12`; there is no direct concrete call site for any of the three. Inside each, the body call (`mysql.go:48`, `postgres.go:47`, `sqlite.go:68`) is `d.db.Close()` on the stdlib `*sql.DB`, not a repo declaration.

**Every other `.Close()` in backend non-test code is stdlib/third-party and does NOT match a repo declarer:**
- `*sql.Rows` — the large bulk (~55 sites across `store/db/{mysql,postgres,sqlite}/*.go`).
- `http.Response.Body` (`io.ReadCloser`) — `internal/httpgetter/html_meta.go:145`, `internal/httpgetter/image.go:25`, `internal/idp/oauth2/oauth2.go:95`, `internal/webhook/webhook.go:156`; also the AWS S3 `output.Body` at `internal/storage/s3/s3.go:96`.
- `net.Conn` / SMTP writer — `internal/email/client.go:90`, `:124`, `:168`.
- `*os.File` / `multipart.File` — `server/router/api/v1/attachment_service_storage.go:148`, `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:362`, `:543`, `:569`, `store/deployment_config.go:134`.
- `io.ReadCloser` returned by `getAttachmentReader` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:281`, `:484`, `:553`.
- `net.Listener` — `server/server.go:117`, `store/test/store.go:67`.
- `*http.Server.Close` (stdlib) — `server/server.go:216`.
- `*sql.DB` in test containers — `store/test/containers.go:149`, `:182`, `:248`.
